summary: This bill prohibits using any federal funds, including from the Claims and Judgment Fund, to pay the President, their relatives, or associated entities for costs from any criminal or civil matter to which they are a party.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits the use of federal funds (including the Claims and Judgment Fund) to pay the President, relatives, or associated entities for costs arising from criminal or civil matters. This directly blocks a category of government expenditures, thereby reducing federal spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or funding mechanisms.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration policy, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or policy.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net funding.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related criminal penalties.
While the bill references criminal matters involving the President, it does not alter sentencing, policing practices, rehabilitation programs, or broader criminal justice policy.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By restricting certain federal expenditures the bill could marginally reduce deficits, but it does not prioritize or address debt reduction as a policy goal.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance funding.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
